title: Thirteen Improved Binary Constant-Weight Codes with Explicit Cyclic Orbit Certificates
summary: We exhibit thirteen explicit binary constant-weight codes improving lower bounds recorded in Brouwer's table, including $A(29,6,5)\geq 333$, $A(55,4,5)\geq 66144$, and $A(62,4,5)\geq 107360$. Their 408,729 codewords are specified by 11,386 orbit representatives under explicitly given cyclic coordinate permutations, together with a standalone reconstruction and distance verifier. All thirteen orbit expansions were checked to agree exactly with the full codeword lists.
comment: 2 pages; 13 explicit constant-weight code constructions with cyclic orbit certificates; ancillary codeword lists and verification software

title: Star decomposition of complete multipartite graphs
summary: We study minimum degree-sum conditions for decompositions into stars of sizes $k$ and $k+1$, where $k\ge3$. Write $σ(G)=\min_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)+d(v))$, and let $c_k$ be the least integer threshold guaranteeing a $\{K_{1,k},K_{1,k+1}\}$-decomposition for every finite simple graph. Using Tarsi's sufficient condition, we prove that $K_n$ admits such a decomposition whenever $n\ge2k$. Together with the obstruction $K_{2k-1}$ of Zhao and Wu, this gives the optimal integer threshold $4k-3$ for complete graphs. For complete multipartite graphs, we establish the sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge9$ when $k=3$ by a finite computational verification and an extension argument. For every $k\ge3$, the complete tripartite graph $G_k=K_{k^2-k-1,k-2,1}$ satisfies $σ(G_k)=k^2-1$ and has no such decomposition. Consequently, $c_k\ge k^2$, even when the class is restricted to complete multipartite graphs. The optimal integer threshold in this class is therefore $9$ for $k=3$. Sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge k^2$ for complete multipartite graphs with $k\ge4$, and the exact values of $c_k$ for general graphs, remain open in this study.

title: The chromatic-AT choosability of Pseudo-Halin graphs
summary: The \emph{Alon-Tarsi number} $AT(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits an orientation $D$ with maximum outdegree at most $k-1$ in which the number of even Eulerian subdigraphs differs from the number of odd Eulerian subdigraphs. A 2-connected planar graph $G$ with minimum degree at least 3 is called a \emph{pseudo-Halin graph} if deleting the edges on the boundary of a single face $f_0$ yields a tree. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the class of pseudo-Halin graphs in which no two interior vertices are adjacent and every interior vertex has odd degree (equivalently, graphs obtained by iterated Hajós sums of wheels with an odd number of exterior vertices). In this paper, we completely determine the chromatic number and the Alon-Tarsi number of all pseudo-Halin graphs. Specifically, by structural induction and the method of $AT$-orientations, we prove that $AT(G)=χ(G)=4$ if $G\in\mathcal{A}$, and $AT(G)=χ(G)=3$ otherwise. Consequently, every pseudo-Halin graph is chromatic-AT choosable.

title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
summary: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

title: Flatness and Tightness in Hypertopes
summary: A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram. A hypertope that achieves this bound is called \emph{tight}. We prove that a hypertope is tight if and only if its diagram $D$ is a forest and, for every pair of types $\{i,j\}$ that is not an edge of $D$, every $i$-element is incident to every $j$-element. This generalizes a previously known result about abstract polytopes. Finally, we describe a combinatorial method and an algebraic method for constructing tight hypertopes.

title: A Density Bound for Muñiz's List Reversal
summary: Muñiz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.

title: Labeled Chip-Firing on Ordered Directed Graphs
summary: We study labeled chip-firing on rooted directed graphs where for each vertex $v$, the children of $v$ are linearly ordered. When a vertex fires, the selected chips are sent to its children in increasing order. We show that homomorphisms preserving these child choices transport legal firing sequences. We then consider the directed lattice $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ and ask which chips can reach a given vertex. We give a recurrence for the smallest reachable label when sufficiently many chips are present and show that consecutive pairing attains this minimum. Finally, we determine the largest reachable label by symmetry and prove that the reachable labels form an interval when the number of initial chips is sufficiently large.

title: New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers
summary: Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey. The last three improve the listed bounds 67, 133 and 72, and for the two 4-uniform numbers also the values 159 and 317 of a recent data deposit. The colourings of 3-subsets are invariant under groups of affine maps $x\mapsto ax+b$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, for $n=37$, 69 and 97, in the last two cases with one further fixed point. Those of 4-subsets live on the projective line over $\mathbb{F}_q$, for $q=199$ and $q=599$, and are invariant under $\mathrm{PSL}(2,q)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$, so each is given by a table of $q$ entries. For 5-subsets we show that, for every prime $q\ge 5$, invariance under $\mathrm{PGL}(2,q)$ forces six points all of whose 5-subsets have the same colour; our colouring is invariant under all affine maps of $\mathbb{Z}_{83}$. By known constructions the bounds give $R(5,5,5;3)\ge 9605$ and $R_k(5;3)\ge 98^{2^{k-2}}+1$, and $R(6,7;4)\ge 2001$, $R(7,7;4)\ge 12001$ and $R(8,8;4)\ge 588001$. The colourings, and programs that verify them, accompany the paper as ancillary files.
comment: 13 pages, 3 tables. The colourings and the programs that verify them are included as ancillary files

title: A refinement of Szemerédi's distinct-distance bound for points in general position
summary: We prove that every collinear triple free set of $n\ge4$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at least $\lfloor n/3\rfloor+1$ distinct distances. This refines the classical bound $\lceil(n-1)/3\rceil$ of Szemerédi that is based on counting isosceles triangles. The refinement is based on treating the diameters separately: they only appear on the convex hull, so for them, we can use the planar diameter theorem and Altman's theorem on distances in convex polygons.

title: \textsc{Max-Cut} on Token Graphs
summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
summary: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields. In this paper, we use skew-polynomial rings to give a new iterative construction of finite semifields. This construction produces large families of pairwise non-isotopic semifields, each of which is $2$-dimensional over one of its nuclei. In particular, we show that this construction method yields semifields not contained in any family of semifields known so far.

title: A note on Turán densities of daisies and hypergraph products
summary: The Turán density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as $π(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}π(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$. This bound is best possible up to the implicit constant by a classical result of de Caen, and it answers, in a stronger form, a question of Ellis, Ivan and Leader, who asked for the case $s=3$. Moreover, we show a related result for matroid basis hypergraphs. We also consider Turán densities of hypergraph products, of which daisies are a special case. The product of two hypergraphs on disjoint vertex sets consists of all unions of an edge of the first with an edge of the second. For the product $\mathcal H^d$ of $d$ disjoint copies of a fixed $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ that is not $r$-partite, we show that $1-π(\mathcal H^d) \rightarrow 0$ exponentially fast as $d\rightarrow\infty$, and we determine the exponential rate in terms of the minimum number of edges in a homomorphic image of $\mathcal H$. This answers a question of Bollobás, Leader and Malvenuto up to a polynomial factor in $d$, and we further address a related question of theirs for products of two different hypergraphs.

title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
summary: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
summary: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

title: A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size
summary: Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.

title: Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
summary: The strong chromatic index $χ_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $θ(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $θ(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $χ_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $θ(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.

title: Note on the random triadic process II
summary: For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process. Korándi et al. proved a sharp threshold probability ${p}= \frac 12n^{ - \frac 12}$ for the propagation of the random triadic process.Tian and Yang complemented those results by considering the final size of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when ${p}=o( n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ α(3-r)} n)$ for any fixed constant $α> \frac 12$.In this note, we further consider the sharp threshold probability $\tilde{p}_r$ for the propagation of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when $r\geqslant 4$. We prove that $\frac 12 n^{- \frac 12}<\tilde{p}_r\leqslant c\, n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ \frac 12} n$ for some positive constant $c$, and conjecture that $\tilde{p}_r= c_r\, n^{ - \frac 12}$, where $c_r= \frac 12(r-2)!^{ \frac{1}{2r-4}}\bigl( \frac{2r-5}{r-2}\bigr)^{ \frac{2r-5}{2r-4}}$.

title: Fixed-opening-set positivity for perfect matchings
summary: For a perfect matching $M$ on $[2n]$, let $P_M$ be the interval order on its edges and let $\operatorname{Open}(M)$ be the set of smaller endpoints of its edges. For an opening set $O$ that occurs for some matching, put $S_O=\sum_{\operatorname{Open}(M)=O}X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_M)}$ and $H_O=ωS_O$. We give explicit Schur and power-sum expansions of $H_O$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and prove that $H_O$ is $h$-positive (equivalently, $S_O$ is $e$-positive). The Schur coefficients count standard tableaux of staggered skew shapes with prescribed entries in the left cells of distinguished dominoes. The Schur expansion follows from a Jacobi--Trudi sign-reversing involution on arrays with prescribed opener positions. For every partition $μ$ of $n$, a coefficient-transfer formula expresses $[h_μ]H_O$ as a positive scalar multiple of an elementary coefficient of the chromatic symmetric function of a clique blow-up of a path. This graph is a unit interval graph, so Hikita's theorem gives nonnegativity. The power-sum coefficients admit a cycle-type autocorrelation formula in terms of the restricted permutations from the Ferrers threshold model and an interpretation by alternating permutations with prescribed valley values and record partitions; we also obtain explicit threshold formulas. Further results include descent-set refinements, formulas for selected $h$-coefficients, and a rim-hook cancellation for the coefficient of $h_n$. These results refine the global matching identity of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.

title: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
summary: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.

title: Distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
summary: The gem is obtained by joining a vertex to every vertex of a path on four vertices. A distance-hereditary split graph is a split graph containing no induced gem. In this paper, we characterize all connected distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1 and determine the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 1. Our result extends previous results on threshold graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1.

title: k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
summary: The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetković in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$. For each fixed $k\geq2$, we also determine the $k$-trees attaining the largest second largest eigenvalue below $1$ and the smallest above $1$. Finally, we determine all minimal forbidden induced subgraphs among $k$-trees with $k\geq 1$, each of which has second largest eigenvalue greater than $1$, but deleting any vertex gives a graph whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$.

title: Positive semidefiniteness of random submatrices
summary: Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction inequality for Rademacher random variables.

title: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
summary: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

title: Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees
summary: A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. When $l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_t=l$, we abbreviate these graphs as $S(t\cdot l)$ and $C_{t\cdot l}$, respectively. Previous results determined $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(t\cdot l))$ for $t\ge4$ [Graphs Combin. 42 (2026) 80] and for $t=3$, in each case for sufficiently large $n$. For $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$, the corresponding extremal graphs are known for $t=2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The sets $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{t\cdot l})$ were also determined for sufficiently large $n$ [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114673]. In this paper, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t))$ for sufficiently large $n$ when the branch lengths are not all equal. Our result for $t\ge4$ also includes equal branch lengths. As applications, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t})$ for arbitrary cycle lengths and sufficiently large $n$. We also determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ for certain linear forests $F=\bigcup_{i=1}^tP_{l_i}$ and sufficiently large $n$. Finally, we apply our main theorems to obtain the known results on outerplanar graphs forbidding matchings or theta graphs for sufficiently large $n$.

title: Real Principal-Minor Detectors: Normal Forms and Regular Parity Lifts
summary: Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ on a finite index set, and let $t$ be the column of diagonal entries of $A$, viewed over $\mathbb{R}$. A real detector of $A$ is a real matrix whose principal minors equal the integer $0/1$ representatives of the corresponding principal minors of $A$. We prove that $A$ has a real detector if and only if it has one of the form $K+tt^T$, with $K$ skew-symmetric and $\{0,\pm1\}$-valued. These conditions are equivalent to the existence of a principally unimodular skew-symmetric signing of the bordered lift matrix of $A$, and to regularity of the parity lift of its delta-matroid. If the graph on the nonempty index set of $A$, with edges given by its nonzero off-diagonal entries, is connected, every real detector of $A$ is diagonally similar to a detector of this form. The proof uses cut-transposes to preserve the prescribed symmetric part up to diagonal similarity, then applies feasible singleton pivots to a minimal counterexample. For ribbon bouquets, the characterization proves Whistler's conjecture. For every $A$ with a real detector, the feasible-set generating polynomial is Hurwitz stable, and the polynomial counting feasible sets of sizes $2i-1$ or $2i$ by $i$ has only strictly negative real zeros and ultra-log-concave coefficients.

title: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
summary: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.

title: Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron
summary: We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular. Its atoms are the $n!$ permutations, and its elements of rank one, which we call pseudo-atoms, are the edges of the permutohedron. Describing ordered set partitions by chains of subsets, the cuts, we show that the rank is modular whenever the meet is above $\bot$, while the join of two distant atoms can have large rank, so that the rank of the join is a metric on permutations. An element has a unique representation as a join of atoms only up to rank one; above it, irredundant representations have sizes ranging from two to the rank, and the redundancy of an element is its number of atoms minus two. The Möbius function is that of an Eulerian lattice, the Whitney numbers are the face numbers of the permutohedron, and the characteristic polynomial has the alternating coefficients of the geometric case, but only $\bot$ and $\top$ are left-modular, so the lattice is not supersolvable. We show that it is CL-shellable, we exhibit EL-labelings for $n\le5$, and we compare the independent sets of Raz arXiv:2307.05005 (v3, Jan. 2026) with irredundant families and with the matroid of the vertices of the permutohedron. Replacing ordered set partitions by partial flags of subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ gives a $q$-analogue, whose Möbius function is $(-1)^{\mathrm{rk}+1}q^κ$, with $κ$ the number of pairs of elements in a common block at $q=1$, and whose characteristic polynomial and Betti numbers are polynomials in $q$.

title: Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns
summary: Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Plücker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.

title: Weak Degeneracy with Availability for Planar Graphs
summary: Every planar graph admits exponentially many proper colorings for any assignment of lists of five allowed colors to its vertices. In this paper, we show that very little beyond degeneracy is needed to prove that this statement holds. In particular, given a planar graph G (but not the list assignment), our argument provides an algorithm consisting entirely of instructions of the following form: ``Color the vertex v using any color c from its list, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' and ``For the edge uv, choose any k colors from the list of u, then color v by any color c from its list that does not appear among these k colors, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' For every assignment of lists of size five to vertices of G, following this algorithm in all possible ways guarantees that at least $2^{|V(G)|/7}$ different proper colorings of G are produced (and at least one color choice is guaranteed to be available in each step). We also show that this result has the following consequence: for every planar graph G, there exists a set $R\subseteq V(G)$ of size at least 0.06|V(G)| such that G can be properly colored from any assignment of lists of size four to vertices in R and lists of size five to the rest of vertices of G. Moreover, these statements remain true even in stronger settings, such as for correspondence coloring.

title: A very robust Ramsey theorem for hypergraph matchings
summary: A fundamental result in Ramsey theory due to Alon, Frankl and Lovász gives an exact formula for the $q$-colour Ramsey numbers of matchings in $r$-uniform hypergraphs: if $n\ge\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})=(r-1)\|\mathbf{t}\|_\infty+1+\sum_{j=1}^q(t_j-1)$ then in any $q$-edge-colouring of $K^r_n$ there is some colour $j$ with a matching of size $t_j$. We show that a very weak quasirandomness assumption suffices for this Ramsey property: we can replace $K^r_n$ by any $r$-graph $H$ on at least $\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})+o(n)$ vertices that is a sublinear connector, meaning that it has no balanced $r$-partite holes of linear size. This generalises the result for $r=2$ (ordinary graphs) that we proved previously using a compression algorithm based on Gallai-Edmonds decompositions. This structure theory is unavailable in the hypergraph setting, so we combine two other proof methods, namely (a) simultaneous optimisation in all colours by clustering vertices using fractional cover weights from LP duality, and (b) local-to-global structure via random sampling and Kahn's matching theorem.

title: Schubert Calculus in the Eye of the Storm
summary: We introduce new combinatorial objects, called storm diagrams, to study the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of complete flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/B$. We consider the quantum product of an arbitrary Schubert class with a modified Hirzebruch $λ_y$-class of a tautological subbundle. We show that its Schubert expansion coefficients are given by the total weights of storm diagrams. As applications, we establish Pieri rules for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of partial flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/P$. Our storm diagrams provide the first combinatorial model for a manifestly positive multiplication formula for partial flag varieties beyond the Chevalley case, with restrictions imposed on only one of the two Schubert classes.

title: Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope
summary: Let $c(n,k)$ denote the coefficient of $r^{(n-1)^2-k}$ in the Ehrhart polynomial of the $n\times n$ Birkhoff polytope. For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that $c(n,k)/c(n,0)\sim n^{3k}/(2^k k!)$ as $n\to\infty$, confirming a conjecture of Stanley.

title: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
summary: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Turán number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Turán number to oriented graphs. In this paper, we investigate the supersaturation results for the directed path $P_k~(k\geq 2)$ and all oriented stars $\overrightarrow{S}_{p,q}~(0\leq p\leq q$), and all oriented paths of order at most four.

title: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
summary: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973). Nevertheless, for more than sixty years this lower bound has not been substantially improved beyond an additive constant. For $k\geq 3$, i.e. girth at least $7$, the best general bound was $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)+2$, due to Bannai and Ito (1981). We show that for fixed girth $7$ and growing degree $d$ we have $n(d,3)\ge m(d,3)+(1-o(1))d/8$. Furthermore, for girth $11$ we have $n(d,5)\ge m(d,5)+Ω(d^{3/5})$. In particular, the excess $n(d,k)-m(d,k)$, for $k\in\{3,5\}$, tends to infinity with $d$ and is therefore generally unbounded, which answers a question of Bollobás from 1978. For the degree/diameter problem we obtain similar bounds. A graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $3$ or $5$ has at most $m(d,3)-Ω(\sqrt{d})$ or $m(d,5)-Ω(d^{3/10})$ vertices, respectively. This answers a question of Bermond and Bollobás from 1981: for every constant $c$ there are $d$ and $k$ such that every graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $k$ has at least $c$ fewer vertices than the Moore bound.

title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
summary: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $°g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope. We show that the Kozlov simplex $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$ is a lecture hall simplex and that every point of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ has a unique chained decomposition into points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$. Hence the lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ are exactly the sums of shifted lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$, the polytope has the integer decomposition property, every lattice point is a Hilbert function when $n\le 3$, and lattice-point counts and Ehrhart polynomials are products of transfer matrices of the kind used in Part II. We determine the codegree of every Kozlov polytope and show that none is Gorenstein for $n\ge 3$. Finally we compare discrete and continuous invariants: the number of Hilbert functions against the volume and the lattice-point count, where we prove Kupreyeva's observed limit for the fraction of lattice points that are $f$-vectors and extend it to every rank. We also compare the centroid and second moments of the Hilbert functions with those of the polytope.

title: Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity
summary: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq δ^2+4δ+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq δ-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq δ-1$ and completely remove the order restriction. Specifically, we prove that $$ q(G) \leq q(B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}), $$ with equality if and only if $G \cong B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$, where $B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n-δ-1} \cup K_{δ+1}$ by adding $k$ edges joining a single vertex of $K_{n-δ-1}$ to $k$ distinct vertices of $K_{δ+1}$.

title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
summary: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing. No periodicity or restriction on the number of radii is assumed; the radii are required only to have a positive infimum and a finite supremum. Following the finite-subgraph exclusion program of Connelly and Zhang, we first restrict the degree-five flowers and their pairings. The remaining exceptional degree-seven corona forces seventeen complete flowers on an unfolded disk with thirty-seven labels. An exact interval certificate excludes their angle equations. A comparison of logarithmic radii on a recurrent network then forces the radii and the three local degree words. We identify the entire triangulation by reducing these words to the square--octagon tiling and showing that its decoration is forced.

title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
summary: A generalized Steiner system $GS(t,w,n,q)$ is a $q$-ary constant-weight code of length $n$ and weight $w$ that has minimum distance at least $2(w-t)+1$ and attains the Johnson-type upper bound $(q-1)^t\binom nt/\binom wt$. For strengths $t=1$ and $t=2$, such systems were known to exist for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions. For general fixed parameters, Liu and Shangguan (J. Combin.\ Theory Ser.~A 209 (2025), 105955) proved that the Johnson-type bound is attained asymptotically, and asked whether it is attained with equality for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying these conditions. We answer this question affirmatively. We prove that, for fixed integers $q\geq3$ and $w>t\geq1$, a $GS(t,w,n,q)$ exists for every sufficiently large $n$ such that $\binom{w-i}{t-i}$ divides $(q-1)^{t-i}\binom{n-i}{t-i}$ for all $0\leq i<t$. Moreover, the system can be chosen so that the supports of distinct codewords intersect in at most $t$ coordinates. Our proof assigns an independent random labelling to every set of $t+1$ coordinates, which turns large support intersections into conflicts in an exact covering problem, and then applies Keevash's decomposition theorem for labelled complexes.

title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
summary: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $Δ^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matoušek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
summary: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
summary: An $[r,n,1]$-graph has $r$ independent parts of size $n$, with a matching between each pair of parts. Yuster conjectured in 2021 that every such graph has a partition into independent transversals whenever $n\ge 2\lceil r/2\rceil$. We prove that there is an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, this partition exists whenever $n\ge\lceil r+A r^{20/21}\rceil$. Thus $f(r)\le r+O(r^{20/21})$, where $f(r)$ is the least $n_0$ such that every $[r,n,1]$-graph has such a partition whenever $n\ge n_0$. In particular, $f(r)/r\to1$, giving an asymptotic form of the conjecture.

title: Dense induced bipartite subgraphs under local sparsity
summary: The study of dense induced bipartite subgraphs dates back to the work of Erdős, Faudree, Pach, and Spencer on triangle-free graphs. In this paper, we study this problem under different local sparsity conditions. First, we prove that for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$ and all sufficiently large $d$, every $K_{t,t}$-free graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph of average degree at least $\log d-16t\log\log d$. This follows from our bound $χ_f(G)\le d/(\log d-16t\log\log d)$ for every $d$-degenerate $K_{t,t}$-free graph $G$, which answers a problem of Allen, Dhawan, and Noel. For triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs $G$, we prove that $χ_f(G)\le(2.85+o(1))d/\log d$, improving the leading constant 4 in the bound of Martinsson and Steiner. So every triangle-free graph of minimum degree at least $d$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph of average degree at least $(20/57-o(1))\log d$. We also extend the study of a conjecture of Esperet, Kang, and Thomassé to graphs containing triangles. We prove that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $d$ and each edge belongs to at most $d/k^2$ triangles, where $k=\lfloor\log d/\log\log d\rfloor$, then $G$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph of average degree $Ω(\log d/\log\log d)$.

title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
summary: Let $n,m,r$ be positive integers with $n\ge 2m+2$, where $n$ is sufficiently large relative to $r$. Alon and Frankl determined the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing neither $K_{r+1}$ nor a matching of size $m+1$. In this paper, we establish a rainbow analogue of their result. More precisely, if $G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}$ are $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on a common vertex set of size $n$, each having more than $\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_{r+1},M_{m+1}\})$ edges, then $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}\}$ admits a rainbow matching.

title: Equality in the clique bound for critical graphs
summary: A graph is $k$-critical if its chromatic number is $k$ and every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable. Gao and Ma (2023) proved that every $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph with $n > k \ge 4$ contains at most $n - k + 3$ cliques of size $k - 1$, and asked which graphs attain this bound. We answer this question by showing that equality holds if and only if $n - k + 3$ is odd and the graph is isomorphic to the join of a complete graph on $k - 3$ vertices and a cycle of length $n - k + 3$. More generally, for $n>k\ge3$, we determine when the size of a nonempty family of distinct $(k-1)$-cliques in an $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph attains the upper bound $s-k+3$, where $s$ is the number of vertices covered by the family. Equality holds if and only if the graph is such a join (with the complete part empty when $k = 3$) and the family consists of all its $(k-1)$-cliques.

title: Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions
summary: We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram. We also obtain a hook expansion of power sums, an explicit binomial reduction to the dual stable rule, and a Grassmannian $K$-homological interpretation of the one-parameter specialization. Finally, we deduce complementary rules for power-sum multiplication in the canonical basis and the corresponding lowering operation in the dual canonical basis.

title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
summary: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

title: An operator $b$-positivity conjecture for Jack characters
summary: Goulden and Jackson defined a Jack deformation $a_{μν}^λ(α)$ of the connection coefficients of the symmetric group and conjectured that these were polynomials in $b=α-1$ with nonnegative interger coefficients. This conjecture was extended to the structure constants of (stable) Jack characters by Śniady. We formulate a stronger operator conjecture: the differential operators $Δ_μ(α)$ that multiply by stable Jack characters should have coefficients in ${\mathbb N}[b]$ in the normally ordered Heisenberg basis $p_ID_J$. We provide numerical evidence, as well as theoretical consequences of the conjecture which can be rigorously proved. Namely, we exhibit two families of $α$-shifted symmetric functions whose associated differential operators are ${\mathbb N}[b]$ positive simultaneously on the bases $p_ID_J$ and $Δ_μ(α)$. These operators correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the Jack transition measure and to the Cartan generators of the affine Yangian $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak gl}_1)$.

title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
summary: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary. Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

title: Large $k$-cross-free families
summary: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
summary: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
summary: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

title: Character-Twisted Sums of Real Quadratic Class Numbers and a Selberg-Type Conjecture
summary: Extending the arithmetic Selberg-zeta function framework studied by Sarnak \cite{Sarnak1982} and Hashimoto \cite{Hashimoto2007}, we study Dirichlet-character weighted sums of narrow class numbers of real quadratic orders and derive explicit formulas according to the scalar, split, ramified, and inert reductions of primitive hyperbolic classes. Our first main result establishes asymptotic formulas for the class number sums associated with the three noninert reduction types and shows that, after multiplication by the corresponding nontrivial even-character weights, their leading terms cancel exactly for every fixed prime $p\ge 5$. Computational experiments across the sampled ranges of levels and geodesic lengths support a substantially stronger bound for the sum over nontrivial even-characters and exhibit systematic cancellation among the scalar, split, and ramified contributions. If this conjectural bound persists over arbitrarily long polynomial ranges, the resulting exceptional eigenvalues-free regions approach the Selberg threshold $1/4$, providing a possible arithmetic route toward a Selberg-type spectral gap.

title: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
summary: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension. This gives explicit flow-box coordinates, closed formulas for hitting times, return times and orbit averages, and a Newton iteration that computes them with quadratic convergence; in dimension one it recovers Mukhamedov's theorem that interpolated orbits are balls. I then show that the analytic maps $g$ congruent to the identity modulo $p^c$, coefficientwise, are exactly the time-one maps of such fields, and that the field is congruent to $g - \mathrm{id}$ modulo $p^{c+1}$. So the interpolated iterates of Bell and Poonen are flows of this kind, and I obtain a quantitative minimality criterion: if the displacements $g_i(x_0) - x_0$ of $d$ such maps span $p^k\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, the group they generate acts minimally on the ball of radius $p^{-k}$ about $x_0$. Where the argument of Cantat and Jang gives an orbit closure containing some open set, this names the ball, at every level $k$ and in every dimension; for $d = 2$ and $k = 1$ it is Jang's criterion for Markoff surfaces, which I test numerically at $7830$ points. Finally, the formal logarithm of $\mathbb{G}_m$ or of an elliptic curve is the rectifying coordinate of an explicit field, so the local divisibility $v_p([t]z) = v_p(z) + v_p(t)$ for $v_p(z) \ge 1 + c$, deep in the kernel of reduction, follows from the metric identity alone.

title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over a quadratic field
summary: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.

title: Self-adjoint skew quartics, symplectic monodromy, and zeta functions
summary: For an odd prime power $P$, let $A_H(P)$ be the number of $a\in\F_{P^H}$ for which the self-adjoint skew quartic $t^4+t^3+at^2+t+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{P^H}[t;σ]$, with $σ(c)=c^P$. We determine $A_H(3)$ for every $H\ge1$ and prove that its minimal constant-coefficient recurrence has order $24$. Local ramification gives the degrees of the Steinberg and regular cuspidal Frobenius polynomials. Duality and finitely many exact counts determine both polynomials. For $P=p^f$ with $p\nmid f$, we construct an explicit genus-$P(P+1)/2$ flag curve whose zeta numerator is the Steinberg Frobenius polynomial. At $P=3$ this identifies the degree-$12$ factor computed above with the zeta numerator of a genus-$6$ curve. For general $P$ the flag curve and the regular cuspidal factors give a rational expression for the counting series. We evaluate the linear coefficients of the two factors by an elliptic-curve point count and express their quadratic coefficients through a single finite-field character sum.

title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
summary: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus. At $p = 17$ and $43$ one Hecke block of the Mordell-Weil group has logarithm divisible by $p^2$ but $p$-adic height of valuation one, and a comparison of valuations in the quadratic Chabauty identity then shows that each CM point is the only rational point in its residue disc, with no computation of the local height at $p$, no basis of the Mordell-Weil group and no equations for the curve. The inputs come from expansions of differentials at CM points and from a formula we prove for intersection numbers of CM divisors of coprime fundamental discriminants under Hecke operators on $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(\ell^e)$ (Theorem 1.3).
comment: 41 pages, 1 figure. Programs and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24061904

title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function II
summary: We apply the elementary arithmetic argument of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689) to binomial coefficients, and obtain upper and lower bounds for Sylvester's denumerant function for arbitrary positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ that sharpen those of Agnarsson. The lower bound is a sum of binomial coefficients; it holds along the multiples of $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ without assuming that a solution exists, and it is greater than the polynomial lower bound of the first paper. In the upper bound the shift of Agnarsson's binomial coefficient is reduced.
comment: 25 pages. Second paper of a series; the first is arXiv:2204.13689

title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
summary: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of André's $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Frăţilă's formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of André's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
summary: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

title: Exceptional zeros for $\mathrm{GSp}(4) \times \mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Yoshida lifts
summary: The aim of this article is to study an exceptional zero phenomenon for the $p$-adic $L$-functions attached to $\mathrm{GSp}_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ in the critical regions (F) and (D). We construct improved $p$-adic $L$-functions by replacing the $p$-depleted Eisenstein family with its $p$-ordinary counterpart. Under a local compatibility hypothesis at the ramified places and classical control for the families, we show that their poles detect exactly the Yoshida lifts whose smaller constituent is dual to the $\mathrm{GL}_2$ representation. The proof compares their residues with distinguished automorphic periods, extending the coherent period formula to the case where one modular form has weight zero. An explicit Euler-factor identity relates each improved function to the usual $p$-adic $L$-function. At these Yoshida points, the vanishing factor cancels the pole, and the resulting value is expressed through the distinguished period and the logarithmic derivative of the ordinary elliptic root. We also discuss the expected factorization along Yoshida families into Hida--Rankin $p$-adic $L$-functions.

title: Large Gaps Between Piatetski-Shapiro Primes
summary: A Piatetski-Shapiro prime is a prime number that can be written as $\lfloor m^c \rfloor$ for some positive integer $m$ and non-integer $c>1$. Li and Pan showed the results for small gaps between consecutive Piatetski-Shapiro primes for $1<c<9/8$. On the other hand, Deshouillers, Drmota, and Müllner showed the large gaps between Piatetski-Shapiro primes although they did not mention it explicitly whenever there are infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes with exponent $c$ using binomial expansion. In this article, we use a different method from theirs, and we obtain the explicit exponent that appears in their paper.

title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III
summary: We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.
comment: 19 pages. Third paper of a series; the first is arXiv:2204.13689

title: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
summary: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $π$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
comment: 50 pages, 1 figure. Code, data and certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24356239

title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
summary: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.

title: Note on the largest prime factors of consecutive integers II
summary: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. We show that a positive proportion of integers $n\leq x$ satisfy\begin{align*} P^+(n-1)<P^+(n)>P^+(n+1)<P^+(n+2)>P^+(n+3). \end{align*} The proof employs Selberg's upper-bound sieve and the multidimensional Selberg sieve developed in the Polymath8b work.

title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
summary: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here.

title: The distribution of greatest common divisors of binomial coefficients and their upper indices
summary: For positive integers $n,d$, let $A_d(n)$ denote the number of integers $0\le k\le n$ such that $\gcd\bigl(n,\binom nk\bigr)=d$, and put $S_d(x)=\sum_{n\le x}A_d(n)$. We prove that, for each fixed integer $d\ge2$, \[ S_d(x)\sim\frac{d-1}{d}\,\mathfrak c\,\frac{x}{\log x}\qquad(x\to\infty),\qquad \mathfrak c=1.526453\ldots \] The key step is to extend the coprimality result of Ford and Konyagin to arbitrary fixed parameters $d\ge2$ and $1\le j<d$, obtaining \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=1\Bigr\} \sim\mathfrak c\frac x{\log x}. \] The zero set of the corresponding Kummer carry function is a finite union of intervals of total measure $1/2$. We combine this property with estimates for small prime factors, Selberg trigonometric approximation, and exponential sum estimates over primes to count simultaneous carry conditions. We further prove that, for every fixed integer $e\ge1$, \[ \#\Bigl\{m\le x:\gcd\Bigl(m,\binom{dm}{jm}\Bigr)=e\Bigr\} \sim\frac{\mathfrak c}{e}\frac x{\log x}. \]

title: $p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps
summary: We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.

title: Exponential generating functions of multiple polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices
summary: We give an explicit formula expressing any finite product of depth-one polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices as a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of shuffle-type multivariable multiple polylogarithms. The proof starts with an exponential generating function. For any fixed positive multi-index $\mathbf{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$, the substitution $z_i\mapsto z_i\exp(x_1+\cdots+x_i)$ in the corresponding shuffle-type multiple polylogarithm yields the exponential generating function for the functions at indices $\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{k}$, where $\mathbf{k}$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^r$. We combine this identity with the shuffle product for iterated integrals at positive indices and compare coefficients to obtain the product formula. The appendix gives an alternative proof using the Euler differential operators $z_i\partial/\partial z_i$.

title: Mahler measures and a cubic Dedekind zeta value in three dilogarithms
summary: A general formula evaluates a three-variable Mahler measure at Heegner points of fundamental discriminant $-d$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod8$, using CM modular forms and ray class $L$-values. Together with the case $d=27$, it proves six identities conjectured by Zheng. The parameter at $d=163$ also occurs in a cubic Ramanujan-Sato series for $1/π$. For $C=\mathbb Q(a)$, where $a^3+2a-2=0$, an exact hyperbolic volume argument expresses the Dedekind zeta derivative $ζ_C'(-1)$ in three Bloch-Wigner dilogarithms. The analogous identity for $C(\sqrt5)$ remains conjectural and is reduced to one explicit Bloch-group equality.
comment: 32 pages. Ancillary files include verification code and certificates

title: Prime-Power Expansions and Boundary Corrections for the Secular Coefficients of Riemann-Zero Windows
summary: We study the secular coefficients of characteristic polynomials attached to finite windows of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, mapped onto the unit circle. Starting from the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula and Newton's identities, we derive a symmetric prime-power model for their generating function. The model carries an explicit boundary factor $(1-w)^{-ΔS}$, where $ΔS$ is the variation of $S(t)$ across the window. The boundary correction is determined by the integer zero count of the window rather than by a fitted parameter. For finite prime-power tails we prove a mean-square identity with an explicit diagonal term and an explicit error bound, using the Montgomery-Vaughan generalisation of Hilbert's inequality. Numerical experiments near $T = 10^6$, on computed but uncertified zeros, show that prime powers up to $Q = 32$, the zero count of the window and the known smooth term reproduce the secular coefficients. The median relative residual energy is $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ for $H = 181$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ for $H = 724$; the means are $2.1 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{-3}$. The error is strongly asymmetric across windows. An exact convolution identity separates a residual, whose measured size does not depend on the boundary exponent, from its amplification by the boundary factor; the measured amplification follows the exponent over eight orders of magnitude. The diagonal prediction matches the measured power-sum residuals within 16% in the tested regimes. Exact identities and finite Dirichlet-polynomial estimates are kept separate from the numerical reconstruction. Extending the mean-square estimate to the true $S(t)$ is open and appears tied to pair correlations of zeros. This note does not propose a route to the Riemann hypothesis.

title: Exact Differential Spectra for Five Families of Power Functions
summary: For a power function over a finite field, differential uniformity records only the largest entry of its differential distribution table, whereas the differential spectrum records every multiplicity and its frequency. We determine exact differential spectra for five families of low-uniformity power functions in odd characteristic, including families previously studied primarily through uniformity bounds. Our methods combine spectrum-preserving exponent changes, factorial moments, intersections of injective images, character sums, and point counts on curves over finite fields. For the ternary family of Yuan, Du, Qiao, and Zhou, we give a fixed-cover formula and an explicit Artin factorization for one pair-intersection cover; its odd-degree counts reduce to traces of elliptic and genus-two curves. Inverse-cubic powers yield a conic evaluation in characteristic five and low-genus trace formulas in larger characteristics. Four ternary branches associated with Dobbertin, Mills, Müller, Pott, and Willems share one complete spectrum governed by an elliptic trace. For the Yan--Han family, an Artin--Prym decomposition gives all multiplicity frequencies and exact differential uniformity, including a planar endpoint. For Felke's family, we express extension-field spectra as one-dimensional character sums while identifying the known prime-field cases. A standalone program independently reproduces the finite-field calculations used in the proofs.

title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
summary: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
summary: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.
